advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish literal read-set/cited paths from configured blast-radius glob PATTERNS so a real filename containing '*','?','[' is content-hashed (not membership-digested).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/read_set.py:62-64 `def is_glob(entry: str) -> bool: ... return any(token in entry for token in _GLOB_META)` with `_GLOB_META = ("*", "?", "[")`
hash_dep_entry dispatches on is_glob: read_set.py:103-105 `if is_glob(entry): return glob_membership_digest(entry, base=base)` else `_hash_file`

Read targets are untrusted LLM tool args: usage_log.py:216 `target = fetch_target(name, getattr(part, "args", None))`; normalize_read_set (read_set.py:120-158) only filters for existing regular files and never rejects or escapes metacharacter-bearing names, so such a path enters the signed dependency set

POSIX filenames may contain '*', '?', '[' — such a real file read/cited by the reviewer would be hashed as a membership digest, which for a literal-with-metacharacter pattern does not cover the file's bytes, so a later content edit is not detected on either the signing or re-check side
advisory.finding: A read-set or cited dependency path whose filename legitimately contains a glob metacharacter ('*', '?', or '[') is misclassified by read_set.is_glob as a glob pattern, so hash_dep_entry computes a membership digest over its match list instead of the file's content hash. Content drift on such a file then goes undetected (fail-open), defeating ADR 0002's per-path drift detection for that file.
scenarios: A ticket with no file_impact whose review reads a repo file named like `conftest_[gen].py` or `q?.py`
A cited path (kind=file) containing a bracket character, which also flows through hash_dep_entry
advisory.suggested_fix: Do not infer glob-ness from arbitrary path text. Restrict membership-digest handling to the known BLAST_RADIUS_ENTRIES set (or tag entries by kind when composed), and content-hash every read-set/cited path unconditionally via _hash_file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end test that signs a no-file_impact manifest with a blast-radius glob, adds a matching file, and asserts `compute_validity` returns `valid=False`/`verdict='stale-code'`.
evidence: test_scoped_set_stays_current_until_a_dependency_moves asserts `attest._rehash(deps.keys(), ...) != deps` rather than driving compute_validity

compute_validity in attest.py:598-618 reads manifest_deps and returns verdict 'stale-code' when drifted — this branch is only reached in tests with `verified: False` (lines 161, 359), which short-circuit to 'unsigned' before the deps comparison
advisory.finding: The change's primary behavioral claim — that a file added under a blast-radius glob after signing (or a drifted read-set path) causes the claim gate to return a `stale-code` verdict — is never asserted end-to-end through `compute_validity`. Scoped-drift tests assert only `attest._rehash(...) != deps` and `hash_dep_entry(...) != before`; `compute_validity` is exercised solely on the unverified/unsigned fail-safe path (lines 161, 359), so the manifest_deps→hash_dep_entry→`stale-code` gate branch (attest.py:598-618) has no regression test.
